title: Dynamic Input Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference on Mobile Devices
problem: SwiGLU-based LLM MLP layers on mobile devices are memory-bandwidth bound, with all weight matrices (up, gate, down projections) fully loaded from DRAM for every token, causing excessive energy consumption and low throughput.
motivation: Mobile devices (Apple A18, Snapdragon) have limited DRAM bandwidth (60 GB/s) and high DRAM energy cost. If input activation sparsity can be predicted and exploited to skip loading irrelevant weight columns at runtime, DRAM traffic and latency can be reduced substantially without accuracy loss.
method: Dynamic Input Pruning (DIP) applies predictor-free top-K selection on MLP input activation magnitudes, selecting only the K largest input elements and pruning corresponding columns of the up, gate, and down projection matrices. No separate predictor network is needed. LoRA adapters can be added for fine-tuning recovery. DIP-CA (cache-aware variant) uses a gamma multiplier (gamma=0.2) to bias selection toward cached weight columns, reducing DRAM refetch. Evaluated via simulation of Apple A18 (60 GB/s DRAM, 1 GB/s Flash) on Phi-3-Medium, LLaMA models.
key_novelty: Predictor-free input-magnitude-based dynamic pruning of all three SwiGLU MLP matrices simultaneously, with a cache-aware variant (DIP-CA) that coordinates column selection with hardware memory hierarchy to maximize DRAM reduction.
contributions: Predictor-free top-K input magnitude selection for SwiGLU MLP pruning
Simultaneous pruning of up, gate, and down projection matrices
DIP-CA cache-aware variant with gamma multiplier biasing toward cached columns
LoRA adapter compatibility for accuracy recovery
46% DRAM reduction and 40% throughput increase on Phi-3-Medium
Apple A18 simulation framework (60 GB/s DRAM, 1 GB/s Flash)

metrics.speedup: 40% throughput increase on Phi-3-Medium on Apple A18 simulation
metrics.accuracy: <0.1 perplexity increase at optimal sparsity ratio
metrics.other: 46% DRAM reduction; evaluated on Apple A18 simulation (60 GB/s DRAM, 1 GB/s Flash)

limitations: Simulation-based evaluation; real hardware results not reported
Accuracy-efficiency tradeoff depends on sparsity ratio and model
DIP-CA benefit depends on cache hit rate and memory access patterns
Currently evaluated on SwiGLU architecture only; does not extend to attention layers
